title: Chiral Central Charge from Real-Space Twist Operator Correlator
abstract: Recent years have witnessed substantial progress in the entanglement-based characterization of quantum phases of matter, with growing interest in real-space formulas due to their theoretical and experimental relevance. For two-dimensional gapped quantum systems, we propose a universal real-space formula for the chiral central charge based on the twist-operator correlator $Z_{g,h}=\langleψ^{(N)}\rvert\mathcal{T}_A(g)\mathcal{T}_B(h)\mathcal{T}_C(g)\mathcal{T}_C(h)\lvertψ^{(N)}\rangle$, where $\lvertψ^{(N)}\rangle=\lvertψ\rangle^{\otimes N}$ is the $N$-copy state and $g,h\in S_N$ are permutations. The twist operator $\mathcal{T}_R(g)$ permutes the $N$ replicas within region $R$ according to $g$. For pairs $(g,h)$ satisfying the spherical condition, we show that the phase of the correlator is determined by the chiral central charge $\mathfrak{c}_{-}$ through $Z_{g,h}/\left\lvert Z_{g,h}\right\rvert=(θ_gθ_h/θ_{gh})^{\mathfrak{c}_{-}}$, where $θ_g^{\mathfrak{c}_{-}}$ is the topological spin of the twist defect labeled by $g\in S_N$. The construction applies to both bosonic and fermionic systems. We derive the formula within a field-theoretic framework under suitable assumptions and further test it numerically in microscopic lattice models. Our results establish a universal connection between real-space entanglement structures and the chiral central charge, providing a systematic framework for characterizing chiral topological phases directly on the lattice.
summary: This work establishes a universal, real-space formula connecting the chiral central charge ($c_{-}$) of 2D gapped quantum systems to the phase of a twist-operator correlator. By analyzing the correlator on lattice models like the QWZ and Kitaev honeycomb systems, the authors provide a systematic, measurable diagnostic tool for characterizing chiral topological phases directly on a lattice.
main_problem: To derive a universal, real-space formula for the chiral central charge ($c_{-}$) in two-dimensional gapped quantum systems.
main_result: The phase of the twist-operator correlator, $Z_{g,h}$, is shown to be determined by the chiral central charge via the relation $ rac{Z_{g,h}}{|Z_{g,h}|} = \left( rac{	heta_g 	heta_h}{	heta_{gh}}ight)^{c_{-}}$.
method: The derivation uses a field-theoretic framework applied to the twist-operator correlator, which is interpreted as a partition function on a constructed surface $\Sigma$.
model_or_system: The theory applies to 2D gapped quantum systems, tested using microscopic lattice models such as the free-fermion Qi-Wu-Zhang (QWZ) model and the Kitaev honeycomb (KH) model.
key_observables: Chiral central charge ($c_{-}$), twist-operator correlator phase ($\arg Z_{g,h}$), and topological spin ($	heta_g$).
important_parameters: The spherical condition on permutations $(g, h)$, and the system size $N$ (number of replicas).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on suitable assumptions within the field-theoretic framework, and the formula is noted to be conjectural for interacting systems.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the twist-operator construction on surfaces (A, B, C) and the construction of the associated genus-three entangling surface $\Sigma$. Numerical results show convergence to predicted values for specific lattice models.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem and the correlator. It then develops the field-theoretic machinery, analyzes the topological constraints via the spherical condition, and finally applies the derived formula to calculate $c_{-}$ for specific free-fermion and Majorana lattice models.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, lattice-based diagnostic tool to measure a fundamental topological invariant ($c_{-}$) using entanglement structures, which is highly relevant for characterizing topological phases in condensed matter systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Twist-operator construction. (a) A large disk A∪B∪ C is divided into three regions, and D denotes its complement. The labels specify the permutations acting in each region. (b) A twist operator supported on a closed region can be deformed to its boundary and then cut open into a twist-defect line. The endpoints (black dots) are twist defects, and the dashed line is the associated branch cut. Depending on the orientation convention, one endpoint is a g twist defect and the other is a g−1 twist defect. Crossing the cut permutes the replicas by g.

FIG. 2. (a) Tripartite region ABC with the four triple points v1, v2, v3, v4. The black lines are the entanglement cuts of this tripartite geometry. (b) The genus-three entangling surface Y is further cut into four three-punctured spheres Yv (v = v1, v2, v3, v4).

The eight punctures are divided into three groups given by the preimages of v2, v3, and v4, which are connected to Σv2, Σv3, and Σv4 by long cylinders. The ramification indices are specified by the cycle types of the relative permutations [gAB], [gBC], and [gAC].
